Description:
A cone and a cylinder that share a common INSCRIBED SPHERE - the pipe fitter's construction. As in
ConesCommonInsphereAtSeam the two surfaces intersect in two plane conics that cross at the two points
where both are tangent to the sphere, so the intersection curve has a NODE there and the two mantles
touch tangentially.

The sphere of radius 10 at the origin is never built. The cylinder about the z axis with radius 10
circumscribes it by construction and touches it along the equator z = 0. The cone has half angle 30 deg,
so its apex has to sit at distance 10/sin 30 = 20 from the origin; its axis is deliberately skew to
everything:
  n = (sin 60 cos 37, sin 60 sin 37, cos 60) = (0.6916386401, 0.5211870984, 0.5)
  apex 20*n = (13.8327728013, 10.4237419686, 10), opening back through the sphere, height 45,
  base radius 45*tan 30 = 25.9807621135
The cone touches the sphere along a circle in the plane n*p = 10*sin 30 = 5; the cylinder along z = 0.
The two circles cross at the two points of the equator with n*p = 5, at the azimuths 91.7356 and
-17.7356 degrees:
  (-0.3028657, 9.9954126, 0) and (9.5247261, -3.0462423, 0)
Both are exactly on the cylinder (radius 10.0000000000) and on the cone (residual 3e-12).

The azimuth 37 degrees of the cone axis is what makes this the OBLIQUE counterpart of
ConesCommonInsphereAtSeam: the cylinder about the z axis is split into half mantles in the xz plane, so
its seams are at 0 and 180 degrees and both nodes lie well inside the faces. The contacts are also at
axial distance 15 of 45 from the apex, so no apex, seam or base plane can help to find them.
Expected:
Exact operand volumes: cylinder pi*100*90 = 9000*pi = 28274.3338823081, cone pi/3*675*45 = 10125*pi =
31808.6256178783. The cone lies within |z| <= 45 - its base circle spans z from -35 to 10 - so the
cylinder caps play no part in the tangential contact, although the cone's base plane does cut the
cylinder mantle transversally, which is a plain non degenerate intersection.

Monte Carlo over the cylinder's bounding box 20x20x90, 4e6 samples:
  intersect        8425 +- 8
  union           51658 +- 8   ( = 28274.334 + 31808.626 - intersect )
  cylinder - cone 19849 +- 8
  cone - cylinder 23383 +- 8
Exact identities: union + intersect = 60082.9595001864 and difference = operand - intersect for both
ways round.
Status:
OK since 2026-08-28. FIXED on 2026-08-28 by the second repair of the same day (Shell.cs, Surface.cs and the new
SurfaceContacts.cs). Two things changed at once and both were needed:
the geometry became RIGHT where it was wrong, and the face partition became REPRODUCIBLE - the case is
stable over 4 runs now, so it finally carries a baseline. Before that it could not be pinned at all:
a face on a periodic surface was split in one run and left whole in the next, and a regenerate run
refused to record anything. The volume never moved even then, which is why the geometry could be
judged while the partition still wandered.

Unlike its seam counterpart ConesCommonInsphereAtSeam this case never had a geometric defect - the
volumes were already right while the partition still wandered - so the fix only had to make it
reproducible. It did:
  coneCylInter  8436.83532065 against 8436.7 +- 1 from a deterministic quadrature (radial solve of the
                cone quadratic at 1440 azimuths, Simpson over z on 600/1200/2400 intervals:
                8435.93 / 8437.35 / 8436.76)
  union + intersect = 60082.39 against the exact sum of the operands 60082.9595001864, 9.5e-6
  coneCylCylMinusCone 11481.7096012 + 8355.69594105 = 19837.41 against 28274.3339 - 8436.8 = 19837.5
  coneCylConeMinusCyl 23063.4567413 + 307.650862246 = 23371.11 against 31808.6256 - 8436.8 = 23371.8

NOTE on the construction, for whoever debugs this: with a half angle of 30 degrees and an axis inclined
by 60 degrees the cone has a HORIZONTAL RULING, because 60 + 30 = 90. Its highest point is therefore
not the apex alone but a whole line at z = 10, and the intersection legitimately reaches z = 10
although the apex itself lies outside the cylinder. That was checked and is not a defect, but it is
easy to mistake for one.
